title: fix(acp): allow harness resets from read-only installations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ACP harness resets failing with `EACCES` from a read-only installation, while preserving sessions stored under the former `<workspace>/state` default during upgrades.

## User Impact

GitHub Copilot, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen Code reset hooks use `acpx/` under the Gateway state directory, honoring `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Other reset-hook failures warn once per harness ID per process; subsequent resets still retry.

**Upgrade behavior:** when no explicit `plugins.entries.acpx.config.stateDir` is configured and the new default is empty, ACPX startup or `openclaw doctor --fix` automatically adopts the old state directory, including its sessions and other files. Set the existing override only to retain the old location. An occupied destination and explicit overrides are preserved. Failed adoption warns with the override to set and retains the applicable legacy path for that process. Inspection errors on an already-used destination preserve that destination.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ACPX session-owner migration module owns adoption for both Doctor and service startup, before runtime storage is opened. It uses the already-declared `fs-safe` move primitive for same-filesystem rename and source-verified cross-filesystem copying and cleanup. Pending/completed markers live in existing plugin state, so completion can recover after a marker-write failure and completed adoption never revisits stale legacy files. Doctor declares both directories for update backup and reports adoption problems as recoverable warnings.

No new configuration, dependency, filesystem sidecar, or runtime cache is added. The migration follow-up adds about 200 production lines for recovery, notices, backup inventory, and both entry points. The existing filesystem implementation owns the actual move.

## Evidence

| Contract | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Five registered reset hooks with a read-only package directory | 5 `EACCES` failures | All 5 succeed |
| Default-state adoption: absent destination, empty destination, cross-device move | All 3 lose session visibility | All 3 preserve readable sessions and remove the old directory |
| Unreadable legacy state or failed move | Both select the empty new store | Both select the legacy path and warn |
| Explicit location or occupied destination | Preserved | Preserved |
| Warnings from 222 failing resets across two harness IDs and registry replacement | 222 | 2; all 222 attempts still run |

Validation uses `blacksmith-testbox`, profile `openclaw-check`. No live Gateway was changed or restarted, and no production CPU or loop-delay improvement is claimed.

- Baseline lease `tbx_01m3dt8j2rjym4jybg7xemah03` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36213239530)): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/acpx/src/service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves legacy sessions at startup'` reproduced **5 failures and 2 passing controls** on the existing PR head. The test runner took 9.85 s after dependency installation and fixture correction.
- Candidate lease `tbx_01m3dtphd09tzt6gr00x6sd3nx` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36213633710)): the five-file focused command passed **61 tests** in **59.32 s wall**. Coverage includes real filesystem moves and ACPX record reads, injected `EXDEV`/I/O failures, process-local fallback, marker completion recovery, owner repair, and registered read-only reset hooks.
- Final lease `tbx_01m3dveky88aa2cpnn7nadhbqf` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36214321206)): **62 focused cases passed**, including the final startup/Doctor marker-precedence and non-creating inspection assertions. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 7472eb3b614ef11aa6a2d939568c60ab9decd3da` passed all 25 core test typecheck groups, extension production/test typing, dead-code scans, and core lint before finding three missing-brace lint errors. After fixing those, the same native command scoped to the five changed extension files passed completely, including extension lint and the remaining architecture guards. The unchanged core-test and docs proof was retained. `pnpm build` passed in **477.78 s**; the full final remote command exited 0 in **13m 40.90s**. The build reported a Control UI startup-size warning (371,740 B gzip versus a 371,332 B limit); this patch changes no production UI source. All leases are stopped.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings after resolving marker persistence, fallback selection, and completed-marker precedence in both startup and Doctor detection.

The Doctor integration fixture covers both automatic adoption and an explicit old location, then loads the retained upstream session from the selected store. Restart coverage also makes stale legacy files unreadable after completed adoption; startup and Doctor must honor the marker. Empty-state Doctor detection must remain non-creating and avoid runtime/ownership inspection.

Measured single-worker file cost: `pnpm test extensions/acpx/src/service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 32 cases in 36.30 s cold wall, including worker-bundle compilation; the final additional Doctor assertions also passed on rerun. The existing Doctor integration file passed all seven cases in 22.64 s wall. `pnpm test extensions/acpx/doctor-contract-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all eight cases in 9.33 s wall. The existing process-backed owner-migration suite passed all 14 cases in 31.38 s runner wall.

Validation recovery: fresh leases required `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Two sync timeouts occurred before test execution; those leases were stopped and replaced. An early cross-device staging error was fixed by reusing `fs-safe`; the assertion ratchet was fixed with an explicit result type.

The first follow-up CI run failed in `check-test-types-core-1` because main commit `9ee2b0b3b6f1` (#158464) moved `ControlUiRootState` without updating a retained-assets test import. Main fixed that in `da8149b8ba7d`; the PR uses that owning fix when merged. A concurrent test-only repair here was backed out with a normal commit to remove the overlap, leaving the final source tree identical to the Testbox-validated migration commit `6bd176e248ef`. The merge was checked without conflicts. GitHub [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36218578968) is **green** on `f63393b110e521a14ff8158fce57e12f1647712d`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, in **995 s** workflow wall time. The PR has **144 passing checks, 48 skipped checks, and no outstanding checks**; it remains open and unmerged.

The type-import failure was also reproduced on isolated merge source `d3f3f2415ef8` using `blacksmith-testbox` lease `tbx_01m3dzaaf8ezc41r5zxqbt53fr` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36217740161)); the repaired UI E2E type graph passed in 10.31 s. The corresponding five-group typecheck stripe, typed lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. This temporary proof checkout and lease were removed.

Focused command:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/acpx/src/service.test.ts \
  extensions/acpx/doctor-contract-api.test.ts \
  extensions/acpx/src/session-owner-migration.test.ts \
  extensions/acpx/harness-reset.test.ts \
  src/acp/runtime/session-meta-doctor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Cross-device and permission failures are injected at filesystem operations; the move, storage, and recovery code are real. Service tests capture the prepared runtime configuration and load records with the published ACPX store. The registered-hook regression exercises real runtime initialization. This is synthetic upgrade-state proof, not a published-updater or production Gateway campaign.
